recommended_output.usage: desktop auth-page background images with dark gradient overlay

composition_rules: main detail in upper and middle area
bottom 30 percent calm and low-detail for overlay text
no important details at extreme edges
works under dark green-to-transparent gradient overlay
text_rules: no large readable marketing headline inside image
Arabic may appear only as small UI content, authentic short words, or abstract text-line texture

negative_prompt: stock-photo feeling, generic classroom photos, Duolingo-like cartoons, mascot characters, fake awards, fake metrics, flags, religious or political symbols, excessive decoration, neon colors, purple gradients, beige-only palette, messy overlapping UI, unreadable large text, English headlines, distorted Arabic calligraphy, random letters, watermark, logo watermark, browser chrome with fake URLs, hands with distorted fingers, busy lower third, harsh shadows, cluttered desk, dark unreadable interface, childish game style

images.title: Clear Arabic
images.label: عربية واضحة
images.prompt: Generate a portrait product visual for Waddeh showing the idea of Clear Arabic. A modern tablet or laptop screen sits on a quiet study desk, angled slightly toward the viewer. On the screen is an Arabic reading interface: a central article card with Arabic paragraph lines becoming clearer and more spacious. Some words are softly highlighted in mint green and pale gold to suggest simplified phrasing and comprehension support. The interface should feel like an actual reading tool, with structured text blocks, subtle controls, and a calm learning workspace. Show layered translucent reading cards or subtle before/after text layers, where the front layer is clearer and easier to read. Use Arabic-like lines or small authentic Arabic snippets only as interface texture; no big readable headline. Soft off-white paper surface, deep green sidebar or header accent, mint highlights. One or two highlighted phrases in the paragraph area. A small unobtrusive level indicator may appear as simple dots or steps, without readable labels. The image should feel calm, focused, and trustworthy. Leave the bottom 30 percent less busy, with darker green tones or soft desk blur for overlay readability. Mood: quiet confidence, clarity, first step into Arabic reading. Avoid generic books-only imagery, students smiling at camera, cartoon mascot, giant text, English UI labels, clutter.

images.title: Bridge to Original
images.label: جسر للأصل
images.prompt: Generate a portrait product visual for Waddeh showing the idea of Bridge to Original. A refined Arabic reading interface displays two related text layers: a clearer Arabic version and a more authentic original version. They are connected by a subtle visual bridge: thin mint lines, matching highlighted phrases, or a soft split-view transition. The screen should show that meaning is preserved while the learner gradually moves closer to the source text. Two Arabic text cards overlap or sit side by side. The left or front card is simpler and more spacious; the right or back card is denser and more authentic. Highlighted segments align between them, suggesting this phrase maps to that phrase. The connection should be elegant, not technical or diagram-heavy. Use deep green and off-white as the dominant background. Use restrained gold to highlight a phrase that changes between the clear and original versions. Include faint connector lines or a soft arc between matching phrases. Interface should look like a real product screen, not a whiteboard diagram. No large readable headline inside the image. No English words. Keep the lower 30 percent visually quiet and readable under overlay text. Mood: progress, trust, preserved meaning, gentle movement toward authentic Arabic. Avoid literal bridge architecture, translation app look, dictionary-only interface, random bilingual text, busy charts.

images.title: Reading Memory
images.label: ذاكرة القراءة
images.prompt: Generate a portrait product visual for Waddeh showing the idea of Reading Memory. A modern product screen shows a learner's saved Arabic vocabulary and reading progress. There are compact vocabulary cards, small mastery indicators, and a reading memory timeline or progress rail. The visual should suggest that Waddeh remembers what the learner has read, which words they are learning, and how their Arabic level adapts over time. Vocabulary and meaning build gently over time. Show saved word cards emerging from a reading document, with subtle connections back to highlighted words in the text. Include small progress markers or level steps that feel mature and restrained. Arabic vocabulary cards can show short Arabic words or abstract Arabic line shapes. Use small badges, progress dots, and memory cards in mint, green, off-white, and restrained gold. The UI should feel useful and real, not gamified. A few cards can float or layer above the reading surface, but keep everything organized. No large readable headline inside the image. No English words. Keep the bottom 30 percent calmer and darker for overlay copy. Mood: accumulated learning, gentle progress, personal reading memory, confidence returning to Arabic. Avoid flashcard app clone, childish trophies, streak counters, fake stats, confetti, busy dashboard overload.
